ai.description: Perrotet’s Vine Snake is a slender, 60–80 cm colubrid. It is bright green with a distinct yellow lateral stripe and a pointed, non-elongated snout. It lacks the elongated rostral appendage of other Ahaetulla.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ahaetulla perroteti* is best distinguished by its exceptionally short, blunt snout and lack of a distinct rostral appendage, unlike the elongated snouts of other Indian vine snakes.
ai.habitat: Perrotet's Vine Snake inhabits the high-altitude shola grasslands and montane forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Perrotet's Vine Snake is primarily diurnal, actively hunting for small lizards and frogs among the high-altitude grasslands and shola forests of the Western Ghats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ahaetulla perroteti* is ovoviviparous, giving birth to a small litter of live young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ahaetulla perroteti* is endemic to the high-elevation shola grasslands and forests of the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically above 1,500 meters.
